| | Peter — I am confident about the future of Oregon because of our state, regional, and local existing and upcoming leadership that I work with every day. **These down ballot races are critically important because these offices not only shape our daily lives and the policies that impact us most — but also serve as a launchpad for emerging leaders to do even more for their communities.** Having the right fit for these roles is essential now and in paving our future. I want to share with you whom I have endorsed this cycle and why, from my perspective, they are needed to lead us into the future. **Metro** [**Oregon Metro Council District 5 – Councilor Mary Nolan**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/85155555/473835765/787789644?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDYvMS84MzU0NSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIwYzFlMmYxYS04YjE0LWVmMTEtODZkMC02MDQ1YmRkOWUwOTYiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=STbmdXC-HfQOIzx79_blRuw5U1rMIEm0v-wVE8DbHms=&emci=a48f5db3-a813-ef11-96f3-7c1e5214dad0&emdi=0c1e2f1a-8b14-ef11-86d0-6045bdd9e096&ceid=29359352)
Nolan has proven to be an effective representative for their district. I appreciate the perspective Nolan brings to the table from their experience in the state legislature, as a non-profit leader, and as a former agency director. Please mark your ballot for Councilor Nolan. [**Oregon Metro Council District 5 – Councilor Duncan Hwang**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/85155556/473835766/-821192395?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDYvMS84MzU0NSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIwYzFlMmYxYS04YjE0LWVmMTEtODZkMC02MDQ1YmRkOWUwOTYiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=STbmdXC-HfQOIzx79_blRuw5U1rMIEm0v-wVE8DbHms=&emci=a48f5db3-a813-ef11-96f3-7c1e5214dad0&emdi=0c1e2f1a-8b14-ef11-86d0-6045bdd9e096&ceid=29359352)
Duncan has been a true collaborator on Council and is diligent in his work both inside Metro and with community leaders throughout the region. I have appreciated his willingness to discuss and listen as well as his asking hard questions and following that up with a solutions-oriented approach to his work. Mark your ballots for Duncan. [**Multnomah County District 4 – Gresham City Councilor Vince Jones-Dixon**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/85155557/473835767/248595838?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDYvMS84MzU0NSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIwYzFlMmYxYS04YjE0LWVmMTEtODZkMC02MDQ1YmRkOWUwOTYiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=STbmdXC-HfQOIzx79_blRuw5U1rMIEm0v-wVE8DbHms=&emci=a48f5db3-a813-ef11-96f3-7c1e5214dad0&emdi=0c1e2f1a-8b14-ef11-86d0-6045bdd9e096&ceid=29359352)
It has been a pleasure to work alongside Vince as a City Councilor. I am truly moved by his commitment to community. What Vince will bring to the Multnomah County Commission is a deep understanding of what it means to work with the residents of a community to change lives. I truly believe that serving at the local level first gives you the unique perspective of how hard it is to move a community together...it is easy to divide and slow things down. Vince showed how to move forward each and every time. His lived experience and understanding of how Multnomah County has underserved East County will provide much needed help to those communities going forward. And one of the nicest websites I have seen! **State Representatives in Clackamas County** [**Annessa Hartman, State Representative District 40**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/85155558/473835768/-718909025?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDYvMS84MzU0NSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIwYzFlMmYxYS04YjE0LWVmMTEtODZkMC02MDQ1YmRkOWUwOTYiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=STbmdXC-HfQOIzx79_blRuw5U1rMIEm0v-wVE8DbHms=&emci=a48f5db3-a813-ef11-96f3-7c1e5214dad0&emdi=0c1e2f1a-8b14-ef11-86d0-6045bdd9e096&ceid=29359352)
A trial by fire applies to this Representative's first term with the issue of tolling. While finding a way to fund transportation projects in this state continues to be a problem, the state DOT should have not saddled local communities in Clackamas County with their proposal to toll everyone crossing the I205 Bridge. Annessa calmly led her District through this tough issue as well as many others. Annessa is a member of the Haudenosaunee, Cayuga Nation, Snipe Clan and brings her lived experience to the halls of the capitol with grace and determination. [**Mark Gamba, State Representative District 41**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/85155559/473835769/-1716105386?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDYvMS84MzU0NSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIwYzFlMmYxYS04YjE0LWVmMTEtODZkMC02MDQ1YmRkOWUwOTYiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=STbmdXC-HfQOIzx79_blRuw5U1rMIEm0v-wVE8DbHms=&emci=a48f5db3-a813-ef11-96f3-7c1e5214dad0&emdi=0c1e2f1a-8b14-ef11-86d0-6045bdd9e096&ceid=29359352)
A true leader for the Oregon Land Use Planning Program, affordable housing, livable cities, safety for all, and a champion in the fight again climate change, Mark has stood up and asked us all to do better. Mark is a true leader and we need him back in the House to carry on the work to make our communities more resilient. [**Daniel Nguyen, State Representative District 38**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/85155560/473835770/-596871406?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDYvMS84MzU0NSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIwYzFlMmYxYS04YjE0LWVmMTEtODZkMC02MDQ1YmRkOWUwOTYiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=STbmdXC-HfQOIzx79_blRuw5U1rMIEm0v-wVE8DbHms=&emci=a48f5db3-a813-ef11-96f3-7c1e5214dad0&emdi=0c1e2f1a-8b14-ef11-86d0-6045bdd9e096&ceid=29359352)
Daniel served with distinction on the Lake Oswego City Council and now I am proud to call him my state representative. Daniel is a business owner and he and his wife are amazing public servants. Daniel is concerned about affordable housing, the economic vitality of our state, and issues of taxation. Daniel is a man of his word and has a heart of gold. Please help send him back with your vote. [**Jules Walters, State Representative District 37**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/85155561/473835771/1728634570?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDYvMS84MzU0NSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIwYzFlMmYxYS04YjE0LWVmMTEtODZkMC02MDQ1YmRkOWUwOTYiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=STbmdXC-HfQOIzx79_blRuw5U1rMIEm0v-wVE8DbHms=&emci=a48f5db3-a813-ef11-96f3-7c1e5214dad0&emdi=0c1e2f1a-8b14-ef11-86d0-6045bdd9e096&ceid=29359352)
Jules is the former mayor of West Linn where she provided stable leadership for a city that has been experiencing a lot of change with population growth. She has shown that same stable, clear-headed leadership in the state House over the tolling proposal on I205 as well as affordable housing and attention to the needs of working families as the economy recovers from the pandemic. Please vote for Jules! **Other elected offices in Clackamas County** [**Chair of Clackamas County – former Sheriff Craig Roberts**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/85155562/473835772/-1864775600?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDYvMS84MzU0NSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIwYzFlMmYxYS04YjE0LWVmMTEtODZkMC02MDQ1YmRkOWUwOTYiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=STbmdXC-HfQOIzx79_blRuw5U1rMIEm0v-wVE8DbHms=&emci=a48f5db3-a813-ef11-96f3-7c1e5214dad0&emdi=0c1e2f1a-8b14-ef11-86d0-6045bdd9e096&ceid=29359352)
Craig was Sheriff of Clackamas County while I was Chair of the Clackamas County Commission. I have found Craig to be an honest man. While we had differences of opinions on how to get to mutually agreed upon outcomes, we worked closely together to rise above the different perspectives and get to solving problems. That's what I appreciate most about Craig. He is a kind man. He cares about the residents of the county. And believes the county government should not be about partisan bickering. Craig is the epitome of non-partisan. I am endorsing Craig because he wants to restore integrity, transparency, accountability, and financial responsibility to the county. I say, Amen to that. Please mark your ballot for Craig Roberts. [**Clackamas County Sheriff – Sheriff Angela Brandenburg**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/85155563/473835773/-1823515619?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDYvMS84MzU0NSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIwYzFlMmYxYS04YjE0LWVmMTEtODZkMC02MDQ1YmRkOWUwOTYiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=STbmdXC-HfQOIzx79_blRuw5U1rMIEm0v-wVE8DbHms=&emci=a48f5db3-a813-ef11-96f3-7c1e5214dad0&emdi=0c1e2f1a-8b14-ef11-86d0-6045bdd9e096&ceid=29359352)
Angela worked her way up in the Sheriff's office and has done a great job managing the department, keeping Clackamas County safe, looking out for your tax dollars, and promoting best practice training to take care of people – the whole person on staff and in the public. I have found Angela to be courageous and committed to making Clackamas a safe place for everyone. Please vote for Angela. [**Benton County Commission — Liz Irish**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/85155564/473835774/277406224?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDYvMS84MzU0NSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIwYzFlMmYxYS04YjE0LWVmMTEtODZkMC02MDQ1YmRkOWUwOTYiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=STbmdXC-HfQOIzx79_blRuw5U1rMIEm0v-wVE8DbHms=&emci=a48f5db3-a813-ef11-96f3-7c1e5214dad0&emdi=0c1e2f1a-8b14-ef11-86d0-6045bdd9e096&ceid=29359352)
Liz has been involved in local politics for a long time. Most recently she was on the Benton County Planning Commission and Budget Committee working on affordable housing and garbage issues. Liz has shown real leadership and would add a much-needed pragmatic and progressive voice to the Commission. She is out and about in the community listening and learning all the time. Vote for Liz. [**Washington County Commission – Commissioner Nafisa Fai**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/85155565/473835775/-1068600968?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDYvMS84MzU0NSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIwYzFlMmYxYS04YjE0LWVmMTEtODZkMC02MDQ1YmRkOWUwOTYiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=STbmdXC-HfQOIzx79_blRuw5U1rMIEm0v-wVE8DbHms=&emci=a48f5db3-a813-ef11-96f3-7c1e5214dad0&emdi=0c1e2f1a-8b14-ef11-86d0-6045bdd9e096&ceid=29359352)
Nafisa has been on the County Commission for the last 3.5 years and has become a strong voice for communities not represented in rooms throughout the region and state, while growing her expertise on transportation and land use planning to be able to provide affordable housing and transportation options for everyone. She has accomplished a lot in a short time and deserves another 4 years. Vote for Nafisa. [**Deschutes County Commission – Commissioner Phil Chang**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/85155566/473835776/1033446422?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDYvMS84MzU0NSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIwYzFlMmYxYS04YjE0LWVmMTEtODZkMC02MDQ1YmRkOWUwOTYiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=STbmdXC-HfQOIzx79_blRuw5U1rMIEm0v-wVE8DbHms=&emci=a48f5db3-a813-ef11-96f3-7c1e5214dad0&emdi=0c1e2f1a-8b14-ef11-86d0-6045bdd9e096&ceid=29359352)
Phil has been a commonsense voice on the Deschutes County Commission. He is super knowledgeable on resources management in central Oregon and has been a key part of negotiations on projects to create resilience in the county. He has also advocated for pragmatic solutions to the homeless issues in central Oregon. Vote for Phil! [**State Senate District – Bend City Councilor Anthony Broadman**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/85155567/473835777/775542366?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDYvMS84MzU0NSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIwYzFlMmYxYS04YjE0LWVmMTEtODZkMC02MDQ1YmRkOWUwOTYiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=STbmdXC-HfQOIzx79_blRuw5U1rMIEm0v-wVE8DbHms=&emci=a48f5db3-a813-ef11-96f3-7c1e5214dad0&emdi=0c1e2f1a-8b14-ef11-86d0-6045bdd9e096&ceid=29359352)
Anthony has worked very hard alongside other Bend thought leaders to effectively manage the growth in Bend from unaffordable housing prices, homelessness, transit, parks, and accessibility to government for all. He is a much-needed voice and perspective in the Senate. He is an attorney and has many tribal government clients which adds to the depth of his understanding of how we need to do a better job as a State working with our Indigenous population and Tribal Governments. **These people will fundamentally impact daily life in our communities and I cannot wait to see what they can accomplish for us.** More soon, _Lynn_ |

clean_body: Ballots have dropped, here’s my take: | | | | Peter — I am confident about the future of Oregon because of our state, regional, and local existing and upcoming leadership that I work with every day. These down ballot races are critically important because these offices not only shape our daily lives and the policies that impact us most — but also serve as a launchpad for emerging leaders to do even more for their communities. Having the right fit for these roles is essential now and in paving our future. I want to share with you whom I have endorsed this cycle and why, from my perspective, they are needed to lead us into the future. Metro Nolan has proven to be an effective representative for their district. I appreciate the perspective Nolan brings to the table from their experience in the state legislature, as a non-profit leader, and as a former agency director. Please mark your ballot for Councilor Nolan. Duncan has been a true collaborator on Council and is diligent in his work both inside Metro and with community leaders throughout the region. I have appreciated his willingness to discuss and listen as well as his asking hard questions and following that up with a solutions-oriented approach to his work. Mark your ballots for Duncan. It has been a pleasure to work alongside Vince as a City Councilor. I am truly moved by his commitment to community. What Vince will bring to the Multnomah County Commission is a deep understanding of what it means to work with the residents of a community to change lives. I truly believe that serving at the local level first gives you the unique perspective of how hard it is to move a community together...it is easy to divide and slow things down. Vince showed how to move forward each and every time. His lived experience and understanding of how Multnomah County has underserved East County will provide much needed help to those communities going forward. And one of the nicest websites I have seen! State Representatives in Clackamas County A trial by fire applies to this Representative's first term with the issue of tolling. While finding a way to fund transportation projects in this state continues to be a problem, the state DOT should have not saddled local communities in Clackamas County with their proposal to toll everyone crossing the I205 Bridge. Annessa calmly led her District through this tough issue as well as many others. Annessa is a member of the Haudenosaunee, Cayuga Nation, Snipe Clan and brings her lived experience to the halls of the capitol with grace and determination. A true leader for the Oregon Land Use Planning Program, affordable housing, livable cities, safety for all, and a champion in the fight again climate change, Mark has stood up and asked us all to do better. Mark is a true leader and we need him back in the House to carry on the work to make our communities more resilient. Daniel served with distinction on the Lake Oswego City Council and now I am proud to call him my state representative. Daniel is a business owner and he and his wife are amazing public servants. Daniel is concerned about affordable housing, the economic vitality of our state, and issues of taxation. Daniel is a man of his word and has a heart of gold. Please help send him back with your vote. Jules is the former mayor of West Linn where she provided stable leadership for a city that has been experiencing a lot of change with population growth. She has shown that same stable, clear-headed leadership in the state House over the tolling proposal on I205 as well as affordable housing and attention to the needs of working families as the economy recovers from the pandemic. Please vote for Jules! Other elected offices in Clackamas County Craig was Sheriff of Clackamas County while I was Chair of the Clackamas County Commission. I have found Craig to be an honest man. While we had differences of opinions on how to get to mutually agreed upon outcomes, we worked closely together to rise above the different perspectives and get to solving problems. That's what I appreciate most about Craig. He is a kind man. He cares about the residents of the county. And believes the county government should not be about partisan bickering. Craig is the epitome of non-partisan. I am endorsing Craig because he wants to restore integrity, transparency, accountability, and financial responsibility to the county. I say, Amen to that. Please mark your ballot for Craig Roberts. Angela worked her way up in the Sheriff's office and has done a great job managing the department, keeping Clackamas County safe, looking out for your tax dollars, and promoting best practice training to take care of people – the whole person on staff and in the public. I have found Angela to be courageous and committed to making Clackamas a safe place for everyone. Please vote for Angela. Liz has been involved in local politics for a long time. Most recently she was on the Benton County Planning Commission and Budget Committee working on affordable housing and garbage issues. Liz has shown real leadership and would add a much-needed pragmatic and progressive voice to the Commission. She is out and about in the community listening and learning all the time. Vote for Liz. Nafisa has been on the County Commission for the last 3.5 years and has become a strong voice for communities not represented in rooms throughout the region and state, while growing her expertise on transportation and land use planning to be able to provide affordable housing and transportation options for everyone. She has accomplished a lot in a short time and deserves another 4 years. Vote for Nafisa. Phil has been a commonsense voice on the Deschutes County Commission. He is super knowledgeable on resources management in central Oregon and has been a key part of negotiations on projects to create resilience in the county. He has also advocated for pragmatic solutions to the homeless issues in central Oregon. Vote for Phil! Anthony has worked very hard alongside other Bend thought leaders to effectively manage the growth in Bend from unaffordable housing prices, homelessness, transit, parks, and accessibility to government for all. He is a much-needed voice and perspective in the Senate. He is an attorney and has many tribal government clients which adds to the depth of his understanding of how we need to do a better job as a State working with our Indigenous population and Tribal Governments. These people will fundamentally impact daily life in our communities and I cannot wait to see what they can accomplish for us. More soon, Lynn | ---|---|--- | | | Paid for by Lynn Peterson for Congress |

Peter, I drove for Uber while I first ran for office. I had bills to pay and no income, so that was my option, and I took it – like millions of people do every day.

Instead of demonizing people for their struggles, we should be lifting the working poor up. We _need_ and _deserve_ representation that looks more like us and has struggled like us, Peter! Hi Peter,
We’re at risk of being outspent by our mega-millionaire opponent David McCormick. He’s spent millions of dollars on TV ads across the Commonwealth, and he has the money to keep doing so from now until Election Day.
[**So Peter, will you make your VERY FIRST contribution today, please?**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/casey-em-20240517-2?refcode=em20240517-2&refcode2=2993_552475_GpUJLq&akid=2993%2E552475%2EGpUJLq) Every single donation, no matter the size, helps us fight back and keep McCormick and the GOP from buying Pennsylvania’s Senate seat.
We know that $5 or $10 may not seem like much, and this may be your first time donating to a political campaign. **But there’s simply too much at stake in this election, and so much at risk if David McCormick wins and helps flip the Senate red, to sit this one out.**
[**Your very first donation will have a real impact, and in order to do everything possible to re-elect Bob Casey, we really do need your help. We’ll put it to work right away powering our campaign. If you’re with us, chip in your very first donation today.**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/casey-em-20240517-2?refcode=em20240517-2&refcode2=2993_552475_GpUJLq&akid=2993%2E552475%2EGpUJLq)

|
# Host Committee Happenings
A Newsletter by the Chicago 2024 Host Committee
---
|
---
| | | | | | | | |
---
|
---
|
## Note from the Host Committee
---
| Welcome back to Host Committee Happenings!
We are only **94** days away from the Democratic National Convention! You can support the convention by giving back to communities across the city during the final days of our Chicago Civic Week of Action with Chicago Cares! Service opportunities are available across a wide range of impact areas through tomorrow evening.
Those interested in working with the Chicago 2024 Host Committee to set up future service projects should email [info@chicago2024.com](mailto:info@chicago2024.com).

---
|
---
|
## Celebrating 100 Days To Convention
---
| | | | | | | | | | Last Saturday marked 100 days until the Democratic National Convention kicks off in Chicago!
Convention officials organized a day of service in Chicago’s historic Pullman neighborhood to mark the occasion with local leaders and volunteers.
---
|
---
| More than 100 volunteers were activated from Pullman to Hermosa to celebrate the milestone of being 100 days out from this summer’s Democratic National Convention. Through hands-on service, participants developed a better understanding of community-supported agriculture and environmental stewardship at Kilbourn Park Greenhouse, and contributed to addressing food insecurity at New Hope Church’s food pantry in the Hermosa community. Chicago Civic Action Week is a week-long series of free volunteer opportunities in neighborhoods throughout the city. Service opportunities are available across a wide range of impact areas through May 18, 2024. Those interested in supporting the Chicago Civic Week of Action can sign up on [Chicago Cares’ website](https://chicago2024.us14.list-manage.com/track/click?u=b2032775a03190d822e2a0e73&id=e2be7c9e4f&e=e789b9d47e).
---
|
---
|
## Security Planning
---
| Law enforcement is currently developing a comprehensive security plan for the convention and will continue to keep the relevant communities informed about any updates. The plan will include information on traffic, road closures, parking restrictions, and checkpoints for perimeter entry.
Make sure you’re informed by taking the following actions now:
* The Chicago OEMC App sends important safety alerts and provides access to all available resources. You can download the app from the Apple Store or the Google Play store.

* NotifyChicago is a city service that texts or emails residents alerts for incidents/conditions such as severe weather emergencies, hazardous materials, traffic impacts, etc. Sign-Up at [Chicago.gov/NotifyChicago](https://chicago2024.us14.list-manage.com/track/click?u=b2032775a03190d822e2a0e73&id=3e7ea8c339&e=e789b9d47e)

* CHIBIZ Emergency Alerts are targeted emergency alerts for the business community through a partnership between the Chicago Department of Business Affairs and Consumer Protection (BACP) and Chicago Office of Emergency Management & Communications (OEMC). Sign-Up for CHIBIZ Emergency Alerts: Text “CHIBIZ” to 6-7-2-8-3 OR visit [Chi.gov/BizAlerts](https://chicago2024.us14.list-manage.com/track/click?u=b2032775a03190d822e2a0e73&id=99d17ab95d&e=e789b9d47e) (case sensitive)

OEMC encourages everyone to report any suspicious objects, persons or any unusual activity by calling 9-1-1 or notifying security personnel on-site immediately.
---
|
---
|
## Youth, Accessibility, and Labor Advisory Councils
---
| The Host Committee [recently announced](https://chicago2024.us14.list-manage.com/track/click?u=b2032775a03190d822e2a0e73&id=90d773abc9&e=e789b9d47e) the formation of three additional advisory councils!
These councils will make recommendations on best practices for youth engagement, accessibility, and labor relations for the upcoming Democratic National Convention. Together with the [Business Diversity Advisory Council](https://chicago2024.us14.list-manage.com/track/click?u=b2032775a03190d822e2a0e73&id=af8607492e&e=e789b9d47e), they will work closely with the Host Committee to ensure regional experts can provide input on the convention planning and decision-making process.
---
|
---
|
## Calling All High School Artists
---
| This week, the Host Committee announced the opening of its “Welcome to Chicago” art competition. The competition will run until June 10, 2024 at 5:00 p.m. and invites any currently enrolled full-time student at any public or private high school in the Chicago metropolitan area to submit original artwork inspired by the prompt “Welcome to Chicago.” Graduating seniors are also eligible to enter.
All submitted artwork will be reviewed by a panel of judges. The winning design will be featured on commemorative memorabilia for the 2024 Democratic National Convention. The winner will also receive two credentials for one day of the convention and a $200 Visa gift card. Finalists will have their artwork featured digitally at official convention events and receive a $100 Visa gift card.
---
| Artwork must be two-dimensional and created by hand without the use of AI or digital image generation. The art can be presented in any medium that can be translated to digital files. Video will not be accepted. All entries must be original in concept, design, and execution and may not violate any U.S. copyright laws. Any entry that has been copied from an existing photo or image (including a painting, graphic, or advertisement) that was created by someone other than the student is a violation of the competition rules and will not be accepted. Entries may not contain any political or partisan content, references to any political party or candidate, or hateful, religious, discriminatory, or sexually explicit language or imagery.
Artwork must be submitted in either .jpg or .png formats to [design@chicago2024.com.](mailto:design@chicago2024.com) The uploaded image must be 300dpi. Entries are limited to one piece of art per student and must include the Student Information Release Form with signatures from the student and parent or guardian. More information can be found at [chicago2024.com/design](https://chicago2024.us14.list-manage.com/track/click?u=b2032775a03190d822e2a0e73&id=6009bbb34a&e=e789b9d47e).
---
|
---
|
## Subcontracting Opportunities
---
| To view the latest subcontracting opportunities from our partners, visit our website: [https://chicago2024.com/rfp/](https://chicago2024.us14.list-manage.com/track/click?u=b2032775a03190d822e2a0e73&id=84c52771c8&e=e789b9d47e)
---
|
---
|
## DNC Vendor Directory and Venue Map
---
| If you're planning to sign up as an available vendor for the convention, make sure to complete the Vendor Interest Form at [chicago2024.com/vendors](https://chicago2024.us14.list-manage.com/track/click?u=b2032775a03190d822e2a0e73&id=c31aa62d54&e=e789b9d47e) as soon as possible.
---
| | | | | | | | | [](https://chicago2024.us14.list-manage.com/track/click?u=b2032775a03190d822e2a0e73&id=741e678905&e=e789b9d47e)
---
| | By filling out the form, you'll have the opportunity to showcase your business to a wide audience and connect with potential customers. Our team will carefully review your submission and add your business to the [Vendor Directory](https://chicago2024.us14.list-manage.com/track/click?u=b2032775a03190d822e2a0e73&id=c1121add23&e=e789b9d47e) and [Venue Map](https://chicago2024.us14.list-manage.com/track/click?u=b2032775a03190d822e2a0e73&id=3af7a248b2&e=e789b9d47e). Don't miss out - submit your form today!
---
| Please note that inclusion in the vendor directory and venue map does not mean the Host Committee, Democratic National Convention Committee, or Democratic National Convention endorse or approve any of the listed vendors. The Directory is offered as a resource to groups and businesses who may need to procure services, facilities, or supplies for their events in Chicago in connection with the 2024 Democratic National Convention, and to encourage the use of local and diverse vendors for those needs.
For questions about vendors, please email [v](mailto:vendor@chicago2024.com)[endors@chicago2024.com](mailto:vendors@chicago2024.com?subject=null&body=null). For questions about venues, please email [venues@chicago2024.com](mailto:venues@chicago2024.com).
---
|
---
|
## Volunteer Opportunities
---
| If you're interested in getting involved with the convention but don't know where to start, consider volunteering! Simply fill out our [Volunteer Interest Form](https://chicago2024.us14.list-manage.com/track/click?u=b2032775a03190d822e2a0e73&id=fba272b1d7&e=e789b9d47e) and we'll be in touch with you soon.
In case you missed any of our volunteer information sessions, you can always watch a replay [here](https://chicago2024.us14.list-manage.com/track/click?u=b2032775a03190d822e2a0e73&id=93b2e619cc&e=e789b9d47e). In the coming weeks we will invite individuals who completed the Volunteer Interest Form to fill out an official volunteer application. Once you complete the application and pass a screening and background check, you'll receive shift assignments. If you have any questions about volunteering, please email us at [volunteers@chicago2024.com](mailto:volunteers@chicago2024.com).
---
|
---
| | | | | | | | | |
## Sponsorship Opportunities
---
| Is your business or organization looking for additional ways to get involved with the Democratic National Convention? Consider becoming a Convention sponsor or partner! Inquiries regarding sponsorships and partnerships should be sent to [development@chicago2024.com](mailto:development@chicago2024.com?subject=Sponsorships%20and%20Partnerships&body=null).
---
|
---
|
## 77 Spotlight
---
| This week, we are spotlighting two communities on the far north and far south sides of the city, **Uptown** and **Roseland**.
---
| 📸 _606 Vision_
---
| The vibrant **Uptown** neighborhood is located on the far north side of Chicago. It is known for its nightlife and well-known concert venues that have hosted some of the most famous musicians of our time, [The Riviera](https://chicago2024.us14.list-manage.com/track/click?u=b2032775a03190d822e2a0e73&id=93d65343af&e=e789b9d47e) and the [Aragon Ballroom](https://chicago2024.us14.list-manage.com/track/click?u=b2032775a03190d822e2a0e73&id=fc0f4800e5&e=e789b9d47e). Uptown also has many Asian dining options, offering a variety of global cuisines for foodies.
**Eat** at [Sun Wah BBQ](https://chicago2024.us14.list-manage.com/track/click?u=b2032775a03190d822e2a0e73&id=33acdbbb4c&e=e789b9d47e), a James Beard Award-winning restaurant that serves some of the best Chinese BBQ in town or [Demera Ethiopian Restaurant](https://chicago2024.us14.list-manage.com/track/click?u=b2032775a03190d822e2a0e73&id=98ce03952a&e=e789b9d47e) for some traditional Ethopian food.
**Enjoy** the sun and sand at [Montrose Beach](https://chicago2024.us14.list-manage.com/track/click?u=b2032775a03190d822e2a0e73&id=a966d17009&e=e789b9d47e).
**Visit** the [Green Mill](https://chicago2024.us14.list-manage.com/track/click?u=b2032775a03190d822e2a0e73&id=b1d39c4963&e=e789b9d47e), a century-old jazz club!
---
| 📸 _Old Fashioned Donuts Inc._
---
| **Roseland** is located on the far south side of the city. It got its name from the beautiful flower gardens in the area that the residents kept. This area flourished during the first half of the 20th century thanks to the Pullman factory. Now, the area attracts many to the [Pullman National Historic Park](https://chicago2024.us14.list-manage.com/track/click?u=b2032775a03190d822e2a0e73&id=c3538afdc3&e=e789b9d47e), the city’s first National Monument, on the border of Roseland. Chicago State University has been located in Roseland since 1867 and some notable alumni of the university include Dennis DeYoung of the band Styx and rapper Kanye West.
**Fun fact:** We hosted our 100 Days Out community service event and celebration at the Pullman National Historic Park. You should go to learn more about Chicago’s labor movement.
**Feast** on [Lexington Betty Smokehouse's](https://chicago2024.us14.list-manage.com/track/click?u=b2032775a03190d822e2a0e73&id=a43180971f&e=e789b9d47e) award-winning Chicago-style barbecue! Our team had a chance to try the food and it was delicious!
**Enjoy** some [Old Fashioned Donuts](https://chicago2024.us14.list-manage.com/track/click?u=b2032775a03190d822e2a0e73&id=3c409462fe&e=e789b9d47e) which has been serving Chicagoans for over 40 years.
---
|
---
|
## Vendor Spotlights
---
| Today we’re spotlighting a woman-owned enterprise who has been at the heart of Chicago’s nightlife scene since 1971. [Lodge Management Group](https://chicago2024.us14.list-manage.com/track/click?u=b2032775a03190d822e2a0e73&id=56dc51828b&e=e789b9d47e) has eight venues in the Gold Coast, River North, Streeterville, and Lincoln Park neighborhoods that are all included in the DNC Venue Map, including The Redhead Piano Bar, Pippin's Tavern, The Original Mother's, and more! The locally-owned and family-operated company has been community driven from the very beginning. Lyn McKeaney and LMG are deeply committed to maintaining the safety and beautification of the neighborhood, and utilize their own resources to keep the streets clean while providing support for various community organizations. Consider booking one of their venues for your convention event!
---
| _If you’d like to be featured in our newsletter or social media channels, please sign up for our vendor directory and email us with your business name, logo, description, and a picture or video that best describes your business._
---
|
---
|
## Staff Spotlight
---
| This week, we want to shine a spotlight on **Marisol Aquino** , our Deputy Director of Events, Small Business, and Neighborhood Activations.
---
| | | | | | | | | | Marisol is a Chicago native, born and raised in Logan Square and currently residing in Humboldt Park. She joined the Host Committee to make a real difference and be a part of an organization that has a positive impact on democracy.
Marisol is a foodie at heart and loves to explore different cuisines. Outside of work, she enjoys spending quality time with her family and indulging in some "Mommy time," whether it's a relaxing spa day or enjoying brunch with friends. Her favorite Chicago activities include trying out new restaurants, attending sports games, and shopping.
It's worth noting that Marisol has lived in other cities but none compare to her hometown of Chicago. For her, it will always be "Sweet Home Chicago!"
---
|
---
|
---
| | | | | | | | | |
### Follow Us
---
| _Thank you for taking the time to read our newsletter. If you aren't already following us on social media, we encourage you to do so. We post all of our announcements, reminders, and ways to get involved across our social platforms!_
---
| | | | [](mailto:press@chicago2024.com)| [](https://chicago2024.us14.list-manage.com/track/click?u=b2032775a03190d822e2a0e73&id=d2f03d9e2f&e=e789b9d47e)| [](https://chicago2024.us14.list-manage.com/track/click?u=b2032775a03190d822e2a0e73&id=8d3b7e2693&e=e789b9d47e)| [](https://chicago2024.us14.list-manage.com/track/click?u=b2032775a03190d822e2a0e73&id=5d91498c7e&e=e789b9d47e)| [](https://chicago2024.us14.list-manage.com/track/click?u=b2032775a03190d822e2a0e73&id=a1210cdabb&e=e789b9d47e)| [](https://chicago2024.us14.list-manage.com/track/click?u=b2032775a03190d822e2a0e73&id=7ba8891d17&e=e789b9d47e)

My Democratic colleagues and I are fighting to take back the House because so much is at stake this November. From gun violence prevention and immigration to the economy, **_everything_** is at stake. both leading up to the primary and since we won the Democratic nomination.

Since Tuesday's win, we’ve received thousands of grassroots donations from
folks who are ready to do whatever it takes to defeat Larry Hogan and keep
this seat blue.

Peter: The GOP is celebrating,
too.

Hogan is Mitch McConnell’s handpicked candidate for this race, and it’s
going to be incredibly difficult to defeat him and the dark money super
PACs behind his campaign.

Friend,
This year has definitely been one of the most challenging in our efforts to protect reproductive rights.
This year's ruling by the Alabama Supreme Court on In Vitro Fertilization (IVF) was an extremist decision that 125 of my colleagues supported, signaling Republicans' relentless efforts to restrict our rights.
The thing is, friend, my opponent is being funded by this same kind of far-right extremism.
In fact, during her very brief tenure in Congress, my opponent sponsored legislation that would've effectively banned IVF nationwide. She not only co-sponsored the Life at Conception Act, a total nationwide ban on abortion with no exceptions, but also celebrated the overturning of Roe v. Wade calling it a "dream come true".
In this race, I'm the only candidate who truly prioritizes our community's needs over the extremist agenda of the rich and powerful.
But with the elections quickly approaching, and our seat being Republicans' top target in the state, we need to ensure a strong coalition of supporters to stand with us against these MAGA extremists.

Vicente Gonzalez
Vicente Gonzalez, a life-long Democrat, is a candidate for Texas’ 34th U.S. Congressional District.
From humble beginnings, Vicente was raised in a military family. Through hard work and pure ganas, Vicente aimed to make something of himself. His mother stressed to him over and over again that education was the key that will open doors of opportunities. Vicente made the decision to get his life back on track by going back to school to get his GED, working and attending classes at community college, and earning his college degree alongside other military families at the Embry Riddle Aeronautical University on the Corpus Christi Naval Air Station. Vicente surpassed his and his parents' dreams when he graduated from Texas A&M School of Law, earning his Juris Doctorate degree.

After law school, Vicente didn’t stop learning, and continued his training in Negotiation at Harvard University School of Law.
Vicente started his business, the Law Offices of V. Gonzalez and Associates, in McAllen and married Lorena Saenz, a former teacher and administrator in Edinburg and McAllen schools. Vicente has focused his practice on fighting for a level playing field for working families wronged by corporations and insurance companies evading responsibility. Through several victories for our community, Vicente recovered millions in tax dollars for South Texas school districts after shady contractors misspent millions in bond money and put our children in physical danger.
Today, Vicente Gonzalez is fighting for our South Texas values in Congress as a member of the Committees on Financial Services and Foreign Affairs and the Select Committee on Economic Disparity and Fairness in Growth. Vicente has stood by our promise to veterans, helping constituents cut through red tape at the VA and working across the aisle to prevent the shameful deportation of our honorably discharged veterans. He’s working to lower prescription drug prices, protect the benefits and healthcare of seniors, and ensure that jobs and opportunities are there for all with the ganas to work.

| | I am pleased to announce that the FAA Reauthorization Act of 2024 has passed and will be signed by President Biden today. While on its face this legislation may appear fairly straightforward, the circumstances in which it passed are rare in today's divided Congress. The FAA Reauthorization Act is the result of months of good-faith work between House and Senate leaders.**I am humbled that during a time of hyperpartisanship, my colleagues in the Transportation and Infrastructure Committee passed the bill with a**** _unanimous_****63 to 0 vote in Committee.** Today, I am celebrating that we came together and ultimately passed a truly bipartisan, bicameral piece of legislation for the good of our country. **Thanks to the FAA Reauthorization Act we will be able to:**
* **Improve Airports:** The Airport Improvement Program (AIP) will provide over $60 billion in grants for planning and improving public-use airports, from Seattle-Tacoma International to regional and harbor airports all across our district and the country.
* **Increase Safety:** Safety technology will be improved across the board, including 25-hour cockpit voice recordings on every commercial airline and the latest airport surface situational awareness technologies to reduce 'close call' near-collisions.
* **Invest in our workforce:** $60 million will be provided for workforce grants to build and grow the talent pipeline of pilots, aviation maintenance technical workers, and aviation manufacturing workers.
* **Increase Accessibility** : Accessibility standards will be raised, with new rules and trainings to reduce damage to wheelchairs and mobility aids and to better accommodate wheelchairs onboard aircrafts.
* **Protect Consumers:** Airlines will be required to automatically refund passengers booked on canceled or substantially delayed flights, and will be required to notify passengers of their right to a refund.

I could not be more proud of this legislation, which will make air travel safer and more accessible while keeping ticket-holders protected — in addition to adding hundreds of good-paying jobs here in Washington state. name: AOC
subject: Barbarism
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez for Congress
body:
#
If we do not assert ourselves and enshrine our rights — and demand healthcare, and education, and dignity — the alternative is barbarism, which is what we are contending with now.
The fact that people are choosing between medicine and rent is barbarism.
The fact that people are worried about whether they will be on the streets every 4 weeks is barbarism.
The fact that every time a person has an ache or a pain, and they’re scared that it could either be a sore joint or cancer, but they can’t find out because they can’t afford the doctor? **This is barbarism.**
If we do not demand — and not only demand, but win — unions, healthcare, wages, and ending endless war, then we will condemn ourselves to barbarism.
I refuse to give up. I refuse to submit myself to that future. That’s not a life.
**And so to live, we have to fight for each other. We have to stand with each other. We have to fight for this vision and this world.**
[If you can, will you make a $5 contribution – or any amount that is meaningful to you – to help power our fight for transformative change? # FROM THE DESK OF LARRY KUDLOW
---
| | Peter,**I am pleased to share with you that The New York Sun, one of my daily must-read papers, is now the exclusive publisher of my regular columns.

I invite you to consider joining the Sun to receive unlimited access to my latest commentary, alongside some of the finest American journalism.

**But there's also far more to what the Sun is building.

As you know, journalism isn't what it used to be.

I've been in the business for decades, and never before have I seen this once noble profession so abused. The major papers are no longer on the side of the American people, and we are right to withhold our trust.

The impact on our democracy is considerable. Without real accountability, the worst actors in government and at corporate institutions have free reign, and patriotic, hard-working Americans are being sidelined and ignored.

The antidote is to join the movement to build a better alternative. That's the American way.

**The charge to restore American journalism is being led by the Sun.** A proudly all-American, principled publication that has plenty of room for conservative thought and conservative writers, the Sun has upheld the highest journalistic standards since 1833. That's 18 years before the New York Times published its first number.**My decision for the New York Sun to become the exclusive publisher of my regular columns was not taken lightly.**

I value their work and have been impressed by their team, but I know they have a hell of a battle ahead. They are the David facing many Goliaths.

They will only succeed if we join with them in this grassroots national effort. Joining the Sun costs as little as a penny a day. I encourage you to sign up today. Every single person counts.

Following the devastating flooding in Vermont last year, it became increasingly clear that mental health care was missing from federal disaster recovery programs. The MEND Act establishes a FEMA grant program to deploy long term mobile mental health crisis units after a major disaster. These units will provide professional counseling, establish peer support networks, and more. The MEND Act also authorizes critical research on the impact of natural disasters on mental health and substance abuse disorders. Natural disasters can be incredibly traumatic, and I’m committed to working across the aisle to secure support for more robust disaster recovery. name: Elizabeth Warren
subject: Republicans are claiming that consumers actually love getting late fees
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Warren for Senate
body:
An update on the CFPB’s new credit card fee rule

| | | [ ](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/216?t=3&akid=2180%2E4032634%2EOerPqp)
---
Do you enjoy getting charged extra fees from credit card companies? Republicans seem to think so. Let’s back up a second. Last year, the CFPB proposed a new rule for credit card companies to cap their late payment fees — no more $30 or $40 fines for being late on a bill unless they can prove that it actually costs that much to process a late payment. This new rule would save Americans an estimated $10 billion a year. Well, Republicans recently introduced a bill to overturn the CFPB’s rule so that the credit card industry can continue squeezing every last dime out of consumers. One House Republican even said “the vast majority of Americans” support these fees. I don’t know about you, but I can’t think of any consumer who loves fees and loves giving more money to their multi-million-dollar bank. You don’t see very many “'I Junk Fees” bumper stickers when you’re driving around. Now, this might shock you, so you might want to sit down if you aren’t already: it wasn’t consumers who were unhappy about this new rule. It was the credit card companies. In fact, they rolled out a massive campaign to try to stop it, claiming that ending excessive late fees would destroy their industry as we know it. They took the fight to Congress, which got us to the “customers love fees, actually” argument. They also took it to the courts, where a Trump-appointed judge just sided with the bank lobbyists. This new rule was going to take effect this week, but this judge blocked it. Let’s be clear: Excessive late fees are designed to wring some extra profits out of someone who’s already stretched thin. They’re a tool that keeps working people down. This fight isn’t over — I’m going to keep working to stop big Wall Street firms from ripping people off. [**Will you add your name to say you support the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau’s crackdown on credit card junk fees? Together, we can push back against corporate greed.**](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/signup/ew-em-latefees/?source=EMZ20H_FIN_E_20240517_V1S1&t=8&akid=2180%2E4032634%2EOerPqp) | [**ADD YOUR NAME**](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/signup/ew-em-latefees/?source=EMZ20H_FIN_E_20240517_V1S1&t=9&akid=2180%2E4032634%2EOerPqp)

Thanks for being a part of this,
Elizabeth

Last year, the CFPB proposed a new rule for credit card companies to cap their late payment fees — no more $30 or $40 fines for being late on a bill unless they can prove that it actually costs that much to process a late payment. This new rule would save Americans an estimated $10 billion a year. Well, Republicans recently introduced a bill to overturn the CFPB’s rule so that the credit card industry can continue squeezing every last dime out of consumers. One House Republican even said “the vast majority of Americans” support these fees. I don’t know about you, but I can’t think of any consumer who loves fees and loves giving more money to their multi-million-dollar bank. You don’t see very many “'I Junk Fees” bumper stickers when you’re driving around. Now, this might shock you, so you might want to sit down if you aren’t already: it wasn’t consumers who were unhappy about this new rule. It was the credit card companies. In fact, they rolled out a massive campaign to try to stop it, claiming that ending excessive late fees would destroy their industry as we know it. They took the fight to Congress, which got us to the “customers love fees, actually” argument. They also took it to the courts, where a Trump-appointed judge just sided with the bank lobbyists. This new rule was going to take effect this week, but this judge blocked it. Let’s be clear: Excessive late fees are designed to wring some extra profits out of someone who’s already stretched thin. They’re a tool that keeps working people down. This fight isn’t over — I’m going to keep working to stop big Wall Street firms from ripping people off. | Thanks for being a part of this, Elizabeth | | | | | | | | | ---|---|---|--- | Paid for by Warren for Senate All content © 2024 Warren for Senate, All Rights Reserved PO Box 171375, Boston, MA 02117 | | This email was sent to dpwillis67@gmail.com We'll miss you, but you can always .

name: Heidi Ganahl
subject: The Mountain Minute: 5/17/2024
body:
Your daily rundown of REAL news for REAL Coloradans.
| | | | [](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
---
**PRESENTED BY[ROCKYMOUNTAINVOICE.COM](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
| | Hi friends,
I hope everyone is able to get out and enjoy this beautiful Colorado weather! Here's a [list](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) of some activities happening around Denver this weekend. This is the Mountain Minute for Friday, May 17, 2024.
- Heidi Ganahl
---
|
---
| | **TODAY'S TOP STORIES**
---
**[Ten bills passed in session, earning some bipartisan support, aimed to address variety of water issues](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** [THE COLORADO SUN](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
Colorado lawmakers gave the thumbs-up to [10 water measures](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) this year that will bring millions of dollars in new funding to help protect streams, bring oversight to construction activities in wetlands and rivers, make commercial rainwater harvesting easier and support efforts to restore the clarity of Grand Lake.

Money for water conservation, planning and projects was a big winner, with some $50 million approved, including [$20 million to purchase the Shoshone water rights](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) on the Colorado River.

Sen. Dylan Roberts, D-Frisco, chair of the Senate Agriculture and Natural Resources Committee, expressed gratitude for the legislature's focus on water issues and for [funding the Shoshone purchase](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.). "This continues to show the state's financial investment in our water future," he said, "and we'll now ask voters to retain even more money from sports betting to continue that funding commitment."
**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
|
---
**[Monument has spent more than $100,000 in taxpayer funds in'political' legal battle](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** [KRDO](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
* The Town of Monument has incurred [over $100,000 in legal expenses](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) from a conflict between Mayor Mitch LaKind and attorney Grant Van Der Jagt regarding alleged misuse of town funds for campaign materials.
* Van Der Jagt's investigation led to allegations of [financial misconduct and sexual harassment](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) against Mayor LaKind, who countered by filing a complaint against Van Der Jagt for exceeding his investigatory role and having a political agenda.
* LaKind's decision to use town funds to cover his legal expenses [without town council approval](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) prompted ethics complaints, adding another layer of controversy to the ongoing legal issues. Despite the backlash and ongoing investigations, Mayor LaKind stands by his actions, asserting they were in the town's best interest and claiming public support.

**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
|
---
**[Cole Finegan stepping down as U.S. Attorney for Colorado](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** [DENVER GAZETTE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
* Cole Finegan has announced his [resignation](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) as the U.S. Attorney for the District of Colorado, effective May 31, 2024. Finegan, appointed by President Joe Biden, has held the position since December 1, 2021.

* His office handled [several high-profile cases](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), including securing a life sentence for a fentanyl dealer responsible for multiple deaths, achieving a conviction for a dentist who murdered his wife in Zambia, and negotiating a guilty plea in a federal hate crime case related to the Club Q mass killings in Colorado Springs.

* In his [resignation statement](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), Finegan expressed gratitude for the opportunity to serve and highlighted the dedication of his team in working towards justice and the protection of civil rights in Colorado.

**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
|
---
**[Federal land managers are planning Colorado's next wild horse roundup, ignoring pleas to stop using a helicopter](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** [THE COLORADO SUN](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
* The Bureau of Land Management (BLM) plans to [use helicopters to remove 85-110 wild horses](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) from Colorado's Little Book Cliffs, despite ongoing criticism about the method's humaneness.
* Alongside roundups, the BLM intends to implement [fertility control measures](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) and trapping to keep the horse population within a manageable range, targeting a growth rate of 2% to 5% annually.
* The BLM is currently [seeking public input](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) on their management plan and continues to face pressure from wildlife advocates and government officials to consider more humane alternatives to helicopter roundups.

**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
|
---
**[Taking a deep dive on the Denver Broncos' 2024 schedule game-by-game](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** [DENVER BRONCOS](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
* The Denver Broncos begin their 2024 season against the Seahawks and face a crucial early matchup with the Steelers potentially featuring [Russell Wilson against his old team](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.).
* The team's performance hinges on a [three-way quarterback competition](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), likely impacting outcomes in games against strong teams like the Buccaneers and Jets.
* [Notable games](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) include challenging encounters against high-profile quarterbacks and strategic matchups in Weeks 2 and 4 against the Steelers and Jets, and tough divisional games late in the season. The Broncos' season concludes with a potentially [decisive home game against the Chiefs](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), which may determine their playoff fate.

**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
|
---
**[COMMENTARY: Counting on Social Security to fund your retirement? Think again](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY RACHEL GRESZLER, [HERITAGE FOUNDATION](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
_In just nine years, the oldest Gen-Xers will reach Social Security 's normal retirement age of 67. But they have a rude awakening when they learn that the program's trust fund is empty, leaving it able to pay out only as much in benefits as it takes from the paychecks of those then working.
_ _
__That 's straight from the Social Security trustees 2024 report. It also notes that without congressional action, benefits will have to be cut by 21 percent across the board--including for those already retired--beginning in 2033.
_ _
__For the average beneficiary, who receives about $22,000 a year from Social Security, that 21 percent cut will translate into a loss of $4,600 per year. As Social Security benefits will grow faster than payroll taxes for the foreseeable future, benefit cuts will reach 31 percent at the end of the trustees ' 75-year projections._ __
**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
|
---
**ONLY ON ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE ⤵️**
**[Barnhart: Learning to live with the uncertainty of parenting](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** **BY FAYE BARNHART** **| COMMENTARY | MAY 16** _The primary educators and caregivers of children are their parents. It actually does not take a village to raise a child, it only takes parents._
**[Devotional: What the Old and New Testament have to say on immigration](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** **BY DRAKE HUNTER | COMMENTARY | MAY 15** _The contributions of immigrants have enriched our country 's strength and diversity, a fact that we should all appreciate. The treatment of immigrants, whether they are legal or illegal, has been a topic of discussion throughout history, including in modern times. Even the Bible has references to this topic._ __
**[Sloan: The greater threat to the planet](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** **BY KELLY SLOAN | COMMENTARY | MAY 14** _George Will recently wrote a rather chilling column, pointing out something so obvious that it has escaped much attention. That is this: while much of the world is obsessed over climate change, to the point of spending trillions of dollars annually, virtually no attention is being paid to another hypothetical scenario, one that is at least as real in potential (if not more so) as climate change and which bears far more immediate and devastating consequences - that is the threat of nuclear war.__****_

As Social Security benefits will grow faster than payroll taxes for the foreseeable future, benefit cuts will reach 31 percent at the end of the trustees ' 75-year projections. | ONLY ON ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE ⤵️ BY FAYE BARNHART | COMMENTARY | MAY 16 The primary educators and caregivers of children are their parents. It actually does not take a village to raise a child, it only takes parents. BY DRAKE HUNTER | COMMENTARY | MAY 15 The contributions of immigrants have enriched our country 's strength and diversity, a fact that we should all appreciate. The treatment of immigrants, whether they are legal or illegal, has been a topic of discussion throughout history, including in modern times. Even the Bible has references to this topic. BY KELLY SLOAN | COMMENTARY | MAY 14 George Will recently wrote a rather chilling column, pointing out something so obvious that it has escaped much attention. That is this: while much of the world is obsessed over climate change, to the point of spending trillions of dollars annually, virtually no attention is being paid to another hypothetical scenario, one that is at least as real in potential (if not more so) as climate change and which bears far more immediate and devastating consequences - that is the threat of nuclear war.**_ Feel like you have a unique story or commentary to share? name: Gene Karpinski, LCV
subject: URGENT: House votes 216-195 to allow Big Polluters to squat on and lock up public lands
body:
__The best thing you can do right now to help block this disastrous bill is renew your LCV membership. |
---

|
DEVELOPING... in a vote of 216-195, House Republicans just pushed through a MASSIVE giveaway of public lands to Big Polluters. Under their bill, virtually anyone, for a small fee, could claim rights to public lands. That means mining companies could pay a small fee to gain absolute rights to occupy and dump waste on public lands in perpetuity.

LCV needs to ramp up the pressure on members of Congress if we're going to prevent this disastrous bill from moving forward. **The only way to do that is to mobilize -- _and fast_. But we need your help to make it happen.**

[We're asking for the help of every LCV member to block this bill. That means _you_ , Peter. Renew your LCV membership right away to help fund our campaign -- every contribution matters, so even $5 makes a big difference.](https://links.messages.lcv.)

Here's what you need to know: If MAGA Republicans get their way, mining companies would have even more unfettered access to our public lands and be able to dump toxic mine waste on those lands. In the worst hands, anyone would be able to lock up public lands, and even prevent clean energy development on public lands, under the false pretenses of mining.

This bill would tip the scales away from our communities, our environment, and our clean energy future -- giving the mining industry even more power to dictate how we use our public lands.

**We 're not willing to sit by and let that happen -- and we know you won't either.** To keep our work going strong, we need to raise $45,000 before the end of the month. If everyone reading this right now were to pitch in just $5, we'd blow through that goal in minutes. _Here 's where things stand:___

# Why Frederick Douglass?
**A Force for Uniting the United States:** Frederick Douglass serves as a powerful symbol for Republicans to promote the values and principles that make our nation unique. He was born into slavery in 1818, but later became one of the leading advocates for reuniting our nation as the Civil War came to an end. His strong conviction in the power of our founding values and constitutional principles, along with his self-learned eloquence, helped guide Abraham Lincoln and the recently formed Republican party to win a second term based on these values and principles. Lincoln faced the daunting challenge of rescuing a nation divided by the Civil War.
**Believed in American Principles:** History tells us that Lincoln's wholehearted embrace of Douglass's message of fighting for and preserving the values that formed our nation was not only the winning message, but also the roadmap for reunification. Today, as our nation becomes increasingly fragmented along political issues and divergent views of our fundamental values and principles of freedom, engaging people based on this former slave's unassailable historical contribution offers the most effective messaging for winning new hearts and minds.
**A Symbol of Republican Values:** Just as Lincoln turned to Douglass for guiding the salvation of America, Republicans can leverage Douglass as a pivotal symbol for fully realizing the greatness of our country. In a historical context, emulating Lincoln and using the impactful legacy of Frederick Douglass serves to open the door to all voters to find common ground and reunite our country.
**Frederick Douglass played a crucial role in the birth of the Republican Party:** The Republican Party was founded in 1854 by abolitionists who aimed to end slavery and advocate for the civil rights of Black people, with Frederick Douglass playing a significant role in initiating the political campaign.

Hi Derek -- it’s Roger here at the DNC. Every year in May, we recognize and celebrate the rich impact of the Asian American, Native Hawaiian, and Pacific Islander communities. But like many from our community, I’m thinking of the AANHPI community all year round. I’m thinking about not only the many contributions we are making across industries, but also the impact we make in political and social change through our growing engagement in politics. I grew up in the immigrant enclave of Woodside, Queens. In 1976, my parents fled China under Mao’s communist regime and settled in New York. Neither of them had finished school beyond third or fourth grade. They both worked multiple jobs, leaving home at 7 AM and returning some 16 hours later. While my parents were providing for our family, my grandparents were caring for my siblings and me. I was not always a model student or a good kid growing up in New York, and like my story, the AANHPI community and our shared experiences are not a monolith. And our varied stories, voices, and lived experiences are what make the Democratic party that much stronger through our representation and the causes we fight for. I’m proud that President Biden and Vice President Harris have been champions in embracing the AANHPI community by combatting AANHPI hate, promoting economic opportunities for small businesses, improving health care systems that often provide care for our elders, addressing housing discrimination while protecting renters, and making sure the AANHPI community is represented across the country -- including in our judicial system. **So today, I’m hoping you’ll join us on our organizing tool, Reach, to share the impact of the Asian American, Native Hawaiian, and Pacific Islander communities.** [**ORGANIZE WITH US**](https://click.act.democrats.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwocBI0mk5vjThU-5C_MyVjPTyDasLEQ-o_PDwLAcPBDSeRyYPDqTkoZUGakI7t9NryG_tUvF_FXym1P2LD47rWzTXp6UnGoW0Zh1x3rNseaXUzKDmOuJKK2Cn2eArgDWWWjsJhWCWlrQQwIBgAaP8pnVW2xR73yM-y-imv18dKgQWWq5JTtueMihAU7MMN9asLUgBSSLmo6ZHG8FjyWTRmjmhf2rJ2o2dDjoyCgzx-B3cxZTePW5jlDXSEMrg8GSn3jtIvAIq8l3PrXqXvQmfxwKtcZmsVXPpcJ_ORBU_hkJl5SaHMsHaGHsfKB5jsmoHWg/46f/pL6iOtpvSAS_etY1_R8Vsg/h0/h001.SQoBEXJno6C8F52YpqmbisfXGV05c3RUpyRRXSqFuJ4) Thanks for being part of the team, Roger Roger Lau / 劉煒
